question: GQ-007
subject: the regression I created an hour ago, found and fixed
what_i_broke: Adding book_external gave the catalogue a second source. Both dedup paths (build-want-list.mjs and ia-title-dedup.mjs) read "from book" only. The next want-list run would have re-offered all 78 books I had just ingested and refetched every one of them from archive.org.
why_it_would_not_have_been_noticed: It fails by reporting "new" with confidence. There is no error, no exception, no empty result — just 78 duplicates presented as fresh finds, and a volunteer-run archive asked twice for the same text.

proof.positive_case: "John Donne, his flight from mediaevalism" -> ALREADY HELD, library_gid johndonnehisflig00molo
proof.second_positive: "The classical tradition in poetry" -> ALREADY HELD, classicaltraditi00murr_1
proof.adversarial_control: "A Book That Does Not Exist In Any Library 99xyz" -> not held
proof.why_the_control_matters: a fix that made everything match would also pass the positive cases. The negative proves the index still discriminates.
proof.ingest_resume: ia-ingest --dry-run now reports "78 already on vault; 0 to fetch"

a_downstream_case_i_did_NOT_force: The passage index keys on gid INTEGER too, and holds 77,540 book bodies. Passage-indexing the 78 new books would require exactly the synthetic-gid decision I refused an hour ago. It stays unindexed and that is stated, rather than solved by inventing ids in a namespace that means something else.
